distinguishing_features: Applies thermal-duty reduction to PCB solder interconnects under power cycling rather than to gas-turbine liner monitoring/derating.
Uses a passive spatial redistribution of heat/current across a 4-pad solder array and modified lead frame instead of sensor-derived thermodynamic inference and active derating.
Targets reduction of local per-joint solder thermal excursion and CTE-mismatch strain rather than an inferred liner thermal-stress index.
Requires a package/PCB geometry change rather than firmware-only use of existing telemetry.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce cyclic thermo-mechanical strain and resulting fatigue damage in PCB solder interconnects during power cycling by lowering the thermal excursion borne by each interconnect.
parsed.viable_reason: As written, the validation imposes the same external thermal cycle on both boards and CTE-mismatch fatigue is strain-driven, so the claimed 75% reduction in solder-joint ΔT from merely adding parallel pads is not physically established/testable.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Given prior art 1's teaching to reduce thermal-fatigue damage by lowering peak thermal excursions, adding parallel solder pads/lead contacts to spread heat is a routine layout optimization rather than an unconventional mechanism.
